items.title: Finite Lorentz oscillator closure
items.statement:
Work in a material rest frame: an inertial frame in whose coordinates each modelled material element has fixed spatial position $x$ and history $t\mapsto(ct,x)$, as defined by the framework's earlier material-closure formulation. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the material region in that frame and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open time interval. The electric field $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, polarization fields $P_\ell:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, and magnetic fields $B,H:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial-vector fields in that frame. At every fixed $x\in\Omega$, require $E(x,\cdot)\in C^0(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and $P_\ell(x,\cdot)\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ for each $1\le\ell\le N$, so the displayed time derivatives are classical. These are time-regularity conditions only; this postulate imposes no spatial regularity, which must be stated separately wherever a consuming field-equation result requires it. In SI, $E$ is in V m$^{-1}$, $P_\ell$ in C m$^{-2}$, $B$ in T and $H$ in A m$^{-1}$.

For a fixed finite integer $N\ge1$, adopt at every material point $x$ the constitutive equations

$$D(x,t)=\varepsilon_\infty E(x,t)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}P_\ell(x,t),\qquad B(x,t)=\mu H(x,t),$$

$$\partial_t^2P_\ell(x,t)+\gamma_\ell\partial_tP_\ell(x,t)+\omega_\ell^2P_\ell(x,t)=a_\ell E(x,t)\qquad (1\le\ell\le N).$$

Here $\varepsilon_\infty>0$ is a constant scalar with units F m$^{-1}$, $\mu>0$ is a constant scalar with units H m$^{-1}$, $a_\ell>0$ are constant parameters with units F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, $\omega_\ell>0$ are constant angular frequencies with units s$^{-1}$, and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$ are constant damping rates with units s$^{-1}$. The parameters are independent of position and time; this is the meaning of homogeneous in this model. The model is linear because all displayed field and oscillator relations are linear with fixed coefficients, and spatially local because the oscillator equation at $x$ uses only the field and oscillator state at that same $x$. The magnetic law has only the constant scalar coefficient $\mu$ and no independent magnetic polarization variable; this is the nonmagnetic oscillator model adopted here.

The word nonmagnetic here means that the oscillator sector has no dynamic magnetic response; the fixed scalar coefficient $\mu$ can still encode a separate static constitutive response. To identify the displayed quantities with the framework's macroscopic definitions, stipulate $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\varepsilon_\infty-\varepsilon_0)E+\sum_{\ell=1}^N P_\ell$ and $M_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\mu_0^{-1}-\mu^{-1})B$. Then $D=\varepsilon_0E+P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\varepsilon_\infty E+\sum P_\ell$ and $H=\mu_0^{-1}B-M_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mu^{-1}B$. This is a constitutive identification in the model, not a microscopic decomposition.

At an initial time $t_0\in I$, the oscillator state consists of $P_\ell(x,t_0)$ and $\partial_tP_\ell(x,t_0)$. For a selected causal zero-past branch, choose an onset $\tau\in I$ and require $E(x,t)=0$ and $P_\ell(x,t)=\partial_tP_\ell(x,t)=0$ for every $t\in I$ with $t\le\tau$. Continuity gives $E(x,\tau)=0$, and the equation gives $\partial_t^2P_\ell(x,\tau)=0$, consistent with the $C^2$ zero extension through onset. For $t\ge\tau$ this branch is the retarded initial-value equation with those data, so its value at time $t$ uses the applied field only on $[\tau,t]$. If $\gamma_\ell=0$, no decaying stationary impulse response is assumed; in particular, this is not an absolutely integrable convolution for arbitrary bounded histories. This postulate does not assert that any actual material realizes the equations.

items.physical_scope: A phenomenological classical Maxwell-Lorentz constitutive model in the material rest frame of the macroscopic electromagnetism framework. It is linear, homogeneous and spatially local, with finitely many electric polarization oscillators and a fixed nondispersive scalar magnetic coefficient. It asserts no microscopic mechanism, material realization or empirical validity; spatial dispersion, nonlinear saturation, moving-media constitutive laws and quantum transitions are outside its scope.

items.title: Drude current closure and collisionless limit
items.statement:
Use a material rest frame: an inertial frame in whose coordinates each modelled material element has fixed spatial position $x$ and history $t\mapsto(ct,x)$, as defined by the framework's earlier material-closure formulation. In that frame, let $E,P:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be the electric field and polarization, and let $V:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a free-carrier current density. At every fixed $x\in\Omega$, require $E(x,\cdot)\in C^0(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and $P(x,\cdot),V(x,\cdot)\in C^1(I;\mathbb R^3)$, so the displayed time derivatives are classical. These are time-regularity conditions only; this postulate imposes no spatial regularity, which must be stated separately wherever a consuming field-equation result requires it. In SI, $E$ is V m$^{-1}$, $P$ is C m$^{-2}$, and $V$ is A m$^{-2}$. Adopt

$$\partial_tP(x,t)=V(x,t),\qquad \partial_tV(x,t)+\gamma V(x,t)=aE(x,t),$$

$$D(x,t)=\varepsilon_\infty E(x,t)+P(x,t),\qquad B(x,t)=\mu H(x,t).$$

The constant scalar parameters satisfy $\varepsilon_\infty>0$, $\mu>0$, $a>0$ and $\gamma\ge0$. Their units are respectively F m$^{-1}$, H m$^{-1}$, F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$ and s$^{-1}$. The fields $V$ and $P$ have units A m$^{-2}$ and C m$^{-2}$. All coefficients are independent of $x$ and $t$, and the equation at $x$ depends only on the state and electric field at $x$; these clauses define the homogeneous, linear, spatially local closure used here. To identify these constitutive quantities with the framework's macroscopic definitions, stipulate $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\varepsilon_\infty-\varepsilon_0)E+P$ and $M_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\mu_0^{-1}-\mu^{-1})B$. Then $D=\varepsilon_0E+P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\varepsilon_\infty E+P$ and $H=\mu_0^{-1}B-M_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mu^{-1}B$. This is a constitutive identification within the model, not a microscopic decomposition.

At an initial time $t_0\in I$, $P(x,t_0)$ and $V(x,t_0)$ are state data. A constant polarization offset is fixed with the Gauss-law data and is not determined by the current equation alone. The branch $\gamma=0$ is the collisionless model; it has no decaying stationary impulse kernel, and its zero-frequency response is not part of this postulate. This is a phenomenological closure, not a derivation of carrier mass, density, collision statistics or any actual material response.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (236-page complete text)
references.locator: §7.6.1, printed pp. 205–206: the phenomenological equation of motion with linear damping, its frequency-dependent conductivity, and the low-frequency DC limit; those source-specific carrier interpretations are not asserted by this closure.

references.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism: An intermediate level course, complete University of Texas at Austin lecture notes

items.physical_scope: A phenomenological classical free-carrier response closure in a fixed homogeneous material rest frame. It is spatially local and linear, with a single relaxation rate and a fixed nondispersive scalar magnetic coefficient; no microscopic carrier-statistics claim is made. It asserts no empirical validity; spatial dispersion, nonlinear response, moving-media laws and quantum carrier effects are outside its scope.

items.title: Augmented energy and passive absorption
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded Lipschitz polyhedron in one material rest frame. Use real SI fields: $E,H,D,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, a free current density $J_f:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, polarization $P:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, and, when present, carrier current $V:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$. Their units are V m$^{-1}$, A m$^{-1}$, C m$^{-2}$, T, A m$^{-2}$, C m$^{-2}$ and A m$^{-2}$, respectively. Let $\varepsilon_\infty>0$ and $\mu>0$ be constant scalar coefficients in F m$^{-1}$ and H m$^{-1}$. Each $u_L,u_D$ is in J m$^{-3}$ and the flux $E\times H$ is in W m$^{-2}$.

Assume Countable Choice, the smooth macroscopic Maxwell material model, and its curl equations

$$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$$

hold pointwise. The smooth macroscopic material model includes continuous free sources and the total polarization/magnetization identifications specified by the Lorentz or Drude closure. Assume $E,H$ are jointly $C^\infty$ pointwise and satisfy $E,H\in C^1(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(I;H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega))$; $J_f$ and each material-current term belong to $C(I;L^2)$. Here $H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ is the real $L^2$ vector fields whose distributional curl is represented by an $L^2$ vector field, with the graph norm. Take Lorentz fields $P_\ell$ jointly $C^\infty$ and in $C^2(I;L^2)$, or Drude fields $P,V$ jointly $C^\infty$ with $V\in C^1(I;L^2)$, so that the stored energies and current terms are finite. Take either one of the following constitutive branches:

1. **Finite Lorentz branch.** For some finite $N\ge1$, $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}P_\ell$, $B=\mu H$, and
   $$\partial_t^2P_\ell+\gamma_\ell\partial_tP_\ell+\omega_\ell^2P_\ell=a_\ell E,$$
   where $P_\ell$ is jointly $C^2$, $a_\ell>0$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, $\omega_\ell>0$ in s$^{-1}$, and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$ in s$^{-1}$.
2. **Drude branch.** $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P$, $B=\mu H$, $\partial_tP=V$, and $\partial_tV+\gamma V=aE$, where $P,V$ are jointly $C^1$, $a>0$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, and $\gamma\ge0$ in s$^{-1}$.

For the Lorentz branch define

$$u_L:=\frac{\varepsilon_\infty|E|^2+\mu|H|^2}{2}+\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\frac{|\partial_tP_\ell|^2+\omega_\ell^2|P_\ell|^2}{2a_\ell}.$$

For the Drude branch define

$$u_D:=\frac{\varepsilon_\infty|E|^2+\mu|H|^2}{2}+\frac{|V|^2}{2a}.$$

The Lorentz density is positive definite in $(E,H,(P_\ell,\partial_tP_\ell)_{\ell=1}^N)$. The Drude density is positive definite in $(E,H,V)$; a constant polarization offset is not part of this energy.

Then the respective local identities hold pointwise:

$$\partial_tu_L+\operatorname{div}(E\times H)=-E\cdot J_f-\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\frac{\gamma_\ell}{a_\ell}|\partial_tP_\ell|^2,$$

$$\partial_tu_D+\operatorname{div}(E\times H)=-E\cdot J_f-\frac{\gamma}{a}|V|^2.$$

If, in addition, the fields satisfy the exact closure-defined PEC branch of the finite-energy boundary model and $J_f=0$, then the total stored energy $U(t)=\int_\Omega u_L(x,t)\,dx$ or $U(t)=\int_\Omega u_D(x,t)\,dx$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing. More generally the corresponding fixed-volume balance includes the work $-\int E\cdot J_f$ and the displayed nonnegative material-loss terms; no claim of conservation without these terms is made.

items.physical_scope: Conditional local energy identities and fixed-volume passive-energy balances for the finite Lorentz oscillator closure and the Drude current closure, in one homogeneous material rest frame under the stated smoothness and finite-energy Maxwell hypotheses. The undriven nonincrease result is for the closure-defined PEC branch. No existence theorem, microscopic explanation, empirical material claim, or energy law outside these constitutive branches is asserted.

items.title: Analytic susceptibility and dispersion restrictions
items.statement:
Use the finite Lorentz oscillator closure in its homogeneous material rest frame. Let $N\ge1$ be finite, with $\varepsilon_\infty>0$ in F m$^{-1}$, $a_\ell>0$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, $\omega_\ell>0$ in s$^{-1}$ and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$ in s$^{-1}$ as in that model. Assume Countable Choice; for the strictly damped integrable-kernel dispersion clause also assume Dependent Choice, as required by the causal-response supplier. For the time convention $e^{-i\omega t}$, let $z$ denote complex angular frequency in s$^{-1}$ and define the absolute oscillator susceptibility, with units F m$^{-1}$, by

$$\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}(z):=\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\frac{a_\ell}{\omega_\ell^2-z^2-i\gamma_\ell z},\qquad \varepsilon(z):=\varepsilon_\infty+\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}(z).$$

The dimensionless transfer function in the causal-response theorem is $\chi_{\mathrm{norm}}(z):=\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}(z)/\varepsilon_0$, so that it has the theorem's convention $P=\varepsilon_0\chi_{\mathrm{norm}}E$ for harmonic histories.

The function $\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is analytic for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$ for every $\gamma_\ell\ge0$. For real angular frequency $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$ away from undamped poles, $\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}(\omega)$ is the scalar multiplier for a harmonic particular solution: if $E(t)=\operatorname{Re}(e e^{-i\omega t})$ and $P_\ell(t)=\operatorname{Re}(p_\ell e^{-i\omega t})$, then $p_\ell=a_\ell e/(\omega_\ell^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_\ell\omega)$ and $p=\sum_\ell p_\ell=\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}(\omega)e$. This coefficient calculation is not by itself a zero-past response to an eternal harmonic input. In the undamped branch the retarded onset solution is specified by initial data and the real poles are excluded; when every $\gamma_\ell>0$, the separately stated integrable retarded kernels realize the same harmonic multiplier.

$$\operatorname{Im}\varepsilon(\omega)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\frac{a_\ell\gamma_\ell\omega}{(\omega_\ell^2-\omega^2)^2+\gamma_\ell^2\omega^2}\ge0.$$

When every $\gamma_\ell>0$, each causal impulse-response kernel is exponentially decaying, satisfies the integrable-kernel hypotheses of the causal-response theorem, and $\varepsilon-\varepsilon_\infty$ obeys its unsubtracted Hilbert-transform relations. When $\gamma_\ell=0$, that oscillator's poles lie at $z=\pm\omega_\ell$ on the real boundary; the transfer function has no pointwise value at those poles, and no pointwise dispersion formula there is asserted. The theorem makes no universal group-velocity bound.

items.physical_scope: Conditional frequency response of the finite homogeneous Lorentz oscillator model in its material rest frame. Upper-half-plane analyticity holds for all declared nonnegative damping rates; the unsubtracted Hilbert-transform relation is asserted only for strictly positive damping, under the exact integrable causal-response hypotheses. Undamped real poles have no pointwise response or pointwise dispersion formula. No universal group-velocity bound or empirical material claim is asserted.

items.title: Drude conductivity, passive energy and plasma cutoff
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the hypothesis carried by the finite-energy Maxwell supplier. Work in a fixed homogeneous material rest frame in SI and standard right-handed Cartesian coordinates with orthonormal basis $\hat x,\hat y,\hat z$. Let $\varepsilon_\infty>0$ be in F m$^{-1}$, $\mu>0$ in H m$^{-1}$, $a>0$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, and $\gamma\ge0$ in s$^{-1}$ as in the adopted Drude current closure. For a spatially uniform harmonic electric field $E(t)=\operatorname{Re}(e e^{-i\omega t})$, with $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$ and $e$ in V m$^{-1}$, consider the harmonic particular solution of the Drude equations, written $V(t)=\operatorname{Re}(v e^{-i\omega t})$ and $P(t)=\operatorname{Re}(p e^{-i\omega t})$, where $v$ is in A m$^{-2}$ and $p$ is in C m$^{-2}$. The frequency-domain response below refers to this harmonic particular solution; arbitrary initial data may add homogeneous solutions, which are not included in these amplitudes. The conductivity $\sigma(\omega)$ is the complex scalar mapping $e$ to $v$, in S m$^{-1}$, and the absolute permittivity $\varepsilon(\omega)$ is the scalar mapping $e$ to the displacement amplitude in $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P$, in F m$^{-1}$.

For every $\omega>0$,

$$\sigma(\omega)=\frac{a}{\gamma-i\omega},\qquad \operatorname{Re}\sigma(\omega)=\frac{a\gamma}{\gamma^2+\omega^2}\ge0,\qquad \varepsilon(\omega)=\varepsilon_\infty-\frac{a}{\omega(\omega+i\gamma)}.$$

The carrier energy density and the loss term in the smooth Maxwell energy balance are $|V|^2/(2a)$ and $\gamma|V|^2/a$, respectively; the energy density has units J m$^{-3}$ and the loss density has units W m$^{-3}$.

In the collisionless branch $\gamma=0$, set $\omega_p:=\sqrt{a/\varepsilon_\infty}>0$ (so $\omega_p$ is in s$^{-1}$). For a source-free nonzero transverse bulk plane wave with real $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ in m$^{-1}$, frequency $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$, and nonzero complex electric amplitude $e$ satisfying $k\cdot e=0$, the Maxwell amplitude equations imply

$$|k|^2=\mu\varepsilon_\infty(\omega^2-\omega_p^2).$$

Thus $\omega>\omega_p$ admits source-free transverse modes with nonzero real wavevectors, while $0<\omega<\omega_p$ admits none with real wavevector. Extending the same harmonic ansatz to a complex wave number $\kappa$ in m$^{-1}$ along a coordinate $z$ in m, the positive-imaginary branch below cutoff gives a transverse mode that decays exponentially as $z$ increases; this is the evanescent meaning used here. At $\omega=\omega_p$ the symbol gives $k=0$, outside the stated nonzero-wavevector plane-wave class; no claim about the separate spatially uniform endpoint or longitudinal plasma oscillations is made.

The wavelength and microscopic-regime qualifications in the source are not generalized here.

items.physical_scope: Conditional harmonic response and transverse bulk dispersion for the phenomenological Drude current closure in a fixed homogeneous material rest frame. The energy statement is conditional on the proved Drude branch of the augmented-energy theorem and the smooth finite-energy Maxwell model. The cutoff applies to nonzero real-wavevector transverse bulk modes in the collisionless branch only; it asserts no interface modes, longitudinal plasma oscillations, experimental validation or microscopic carrier theory.

title: Causal oscillator media and passivity — Examples

items.title: Phase and group speeds are not causal fronts
items.statement:
Take the finite Lorentz response with $\varepsilon_\infty=\varepsilon_0$, $\mu=\mu_0$, one oscillator $a=\varepsilon_0\omega_0^2$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$, and damping $\gamma=\omega_0/2$ in s$^{-1}$, where $\omega_0>0$ is an angular frequency in s$^{-1}$. For angular frequency $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$, let $\nu=\omega/\omega_0$; its relative absolute permittivity is

$$Z(\nu):=\frac{\varepsilon(\omega)}{\varepsilon_0}=1+\frac{1}{1-\nu^2-i\nu/2}.$$

For each $\nu>0$, define $n(\nu)$ to be the dimensionless square root of $Z(\nu)$ with positive real and positive imaginary parts, and define the complex wave number $k(\omega):=(\omega/c)n(\omega/\omega_0)$ in m$^{-1}$ for a harmonic field with spatial factor $e^{ikz}$, where $z$ is in m, $c$ is in m s$^{-1}$, and $+z$ is the propagation direction. Use standard right-handed Cartesian coordinates $(\hat x,\hat y,\hat z)$ and let $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$. Fix a real amplitude $E_0>0$ in V m$^{-1}$ and, with the real-part plane-wave convention, explicitly extended here to complex $k$, define the fields

$$E_\omega(x,y,z,t)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(E_0\hat x\,e^{i(k(\omega)z-\omega t)}\right),\qquad B_\omega(x,y,z,t)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{k(\omega)E_0}{\omega}\hat y\,e^{i(k(\omega)z-\omega t)}\right).$$

These are real $C^\infty$ maps $\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$. Set $H_\omega=B_\omega/\mu_0$ and

$$D_\omega(x,y,z,t)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\varepsilon(\omega)E_0\hat x\,e^{i(k(\omega)z-\omega t)}\right),$$

the harmonic particular displacement response specified by the Lorentz susceptibility theorem. This is a formal source-free transverse bulk mode; no boundary condition or finite-energy property is asserted. The imaginary part of $k$ gives attenuation along $+z$. Define the narrowband group-delay derivative per unit length to be $d\,\operatorname{Re}k/d\omega$ in s m$^{-1}$; it is a local derivative of phase with respect to angular frequency. For a real temporal signal $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, define its support by $\operatorname{supp}f:=\overline{\{t\in\mathbb R:f(t)\ne0\}}$; if this support is nonempty and bounded below, its front time is $\inf\operatorname{supp}f$. The nonzero harmonic histories at each fixed spatial point are eternal and have support $\mathbb R$, hence have no front time. At $\nu=1$, the group-delay derivative is negative. This derivative does not by itself determine a pulse's support front, which is a property of its full time-dependent signal.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (236-page complete text)
references.locator: §7.5.2–§7.5.3, printed pp. 194–199: phase and group quantities in dispersive media and the damped-oscillator response. The local calculation uses the lossy complex wave number and does not identify its phase derivative with a causal front.

items.physical_scope: An exact narrowband dispersion calculation for one passive, damped Lorentz medium at a specified frequency. It shows that the local derivative of the real wave-number phase can be negative in this lossy model; it assigns no signal-front speed, energy velocity, empirical observation or universal group-velocity bound.

items.title: Matter energy survives zero instantaneous polarization
items.statement: In the one-oscillator Lorentz model, take an undamped oscillator $\gamma=0$ with $a>0$ in F m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$ and $\omega_0>0$ in s$^{-1}$. At a time $t_0$, compare two allowed states with the same instantaneous fields $E=0$, $B=0$, $H=0$, polarization $P=0$, and therefore displacement $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P=0$: in the first state set $P_t=0$, and in the second set $P_t=v$ for any fixed nonzero real vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ in A m$^{-2}$. The second state has oscillator energy density $|v|^2/(2a)>0$ in J m$^{-3}$, while the first has zero oscillator energy. Thus the instantaneous pair $(E,D)$ alone does not determine the full stored energy in this dispersive model.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (236-page complete text)
references.locator: §7.5.1, printed pp. 193–194: the atom's polarization is the state of a forced oscillator; the positive stored-energy comparison here is derived from the local model theorem.

references.locator: Slides 8–13 (PDF pp. 8–13): oscillator state, damping and polarization response. The example's equal-(E,D), unequal-energy comparison is derived from the local augmented-energy theorem; the source is contextual only.

items.physical_scope: A single allowed oscillator state in the undamped Lorentz model. It illustrates the model's positive kinetic material-energy term when the instantaneous polarization vanishes; it reports no experiment and makes no claim beyond the stated constitutive model.
